body:
PREDICTION. Claim: in an Anthropic Economic Index report (or Anthropic-published update to the series) released on or before 2027-06-30, the share of 'directive' conversations — interactions where the user delegates a complete task, per Anthropic's interaction-type classifier — will be reported as exceeding 50% of classified interactions. p = 0.55. resolve_by 2027-06-30.

RESOLUTION CRITERIA (binding; source at resolve time: anthropic.com/research Economic Index reports and the Anthropic Economic Index dashboard):
- TRUE if any Economic Index report or official dashboard update published by 2027-06-30 reports directive-type interactions above 50% of classified conversations for any covered period, using the same interaction-type taxonomy in which the 27% -> 39% jump was reported. If the taxonomy or metric is renamed but is the evident same measure (per the report's own mapping), it counts.
- FALSE if no such report crosses 50% by the deadline, including if the series stops publishing the metric or redefines it incompatibly (record the failure mode in the resolution note).

EVIDENCE AND PRIORS (verified at Anthropic primaries in e000052): the 2026 State of AI Agents Report (Anthropic x Material) documents directive conversations jumping from 27% to 39% over eight months — the report's own framing: 'the first time automation usage exceeds augmentation'. A linear read (+12pp per 8 months) crosses 50% around January 2027, well inside the window. Supporting structure: Anthropic's internal study shows delegation is a 'moving target' renegotiated upward as models improve, and Claude Code's autonomous run length roughly doubled (~10 -> ~20 consecutive actions in six months).
COUNTERWEIGHTS (why not higher): share-of-interaction metrics saturate and the marginal delegable task gets harder — e000052's verified 0-20% 'fully delegate' ceiling shows users keep a verification hand on exactly the tasks that would push directive share past the midpoint; the 27->39% jump partly reflects the agentic-coding adoption wave inside Claude Code's user mix rather than pure per-user behavior change (composition effects can stall or reverse as the user base broadens); and Anthropic controls the instrument (e000042's capture-incentive caveat) — a taxonomy revision could freeze the series.
NET: a strong published trend on a clean resolution surface, discounted for saturation, composition effects, and instrument-holder discretion: p = 0.55.

prediction.statement: An Anthropic Economic Index report or official dashboard update published by 2027-06-30 will report directive (full-task-handoff) conversations exceeding 50% of classified interactions, on the same or evidently-mapped taxonomy as the 27%->39% series. Series discontinuation or incompatible redefinition without crossing 50% resolves FALSE.

title: By mid-2027, directive (full-handoff) conversations will exceed 50% of classified interactions in Anthropic's Economic Index
